e: Bangladesh boxer Hamza Uddin won the British Flyweight Championship in Boxing.
A bus crushes an auto-rickshaw, killing seven people in Mymensingh.
The July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum is inaugurated by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Mohammed Shahabuddin resigns as President of Bangladesh citing ill health.
The United States imposes a 10% tariff on Bangladesh, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.
At least 51 people are reported killed following days of flooding caused by heavy rains nationwide.

The high profile quadruple murder of a mother and her three daughters by fruit vendor Antar Majumdar at their own house in Lakshmipur District. Antar Majumdar is killed on the same day by an enraged mob.
A magnitude 4.4 earthquake hits Dhaka Division, injuring one person.
A truck plunges into a ditch between Dhaka and Tangail, killing 15 and injuring 10.
Foreign minister Khalilur Rahman is elected as president of the United Nations General Assembly.
A truck carrying iron rods and hitchhikers overturns in Tangail District, killing 15 people and wounding 10.
Veteran Cricketer Mushfiqur Rahim's century leads Bangladesh to a historic Test cricket series win against Pakistan.
Babar Ali becomes the first Bangladeshi to climb Mount Makalu.

A trawler carrying migrants capsizes in the Andaman Sea on its way to Malaysia from Teknaf, Cox's Bazar District, leaving 250 passengers missing. Nine people are rescued by the Bangladeshi-flagged vessel M.T. Meghna Pride.
Bangladesh launches an emergency MMR vaccine campaign after new health data shows that at least 130 children have been reported dead from measles in the last six weeks.
Five people are killed in a fire at a gas lighter factory in Keraniganj Upazila, Dhaka District.
Five people, including a child are killed after being run over by a train in Dholatengor, Kalihati Upazila, Tangail District.
At least 26 people are killed, 11 others survive and six are reported missing when a passenger bus plunges into the Padma River in Goalanda Upazila, Rajbari District, Dhaka Division.
A train collides with a bus in Paduar Bazar rail crossing, Comilla Sadar Dakshin Upazila, Comilla District, killing 12 people and injuring at least 15 others.
A launch is rear-ended by another launch while picking up passengers in Sadarghat Launch Terminal in Dhaka, killing two people, injuring a pregnant woman and leaving three missing.
Hafiz Uddin Ahmad is elected as speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad.
A Bangladesh Navy bus collides with a microbus carrying wedding guests in Rampal Upazila, Bagerhat District, killing 14 people including 11 from same family with bridegroom and injuring several.
The government closes all universities and imposes fuel rationing due to energy shortages caused by the 2026 Iran war.
Three people, including a Purohita, are injured in a firebombing at a temple in Comilla.
A fugitive murderer named Mir Hossain is arrested by a PBI investigating officer for the killing of a Hindu woman, Rekha Rani Roy, from Monshiganj in 2024.
A woman cuts off a sex harasser's penis with a blade during attempted rape in Joypurhat.
A court in Dhaka orders the government to petition Interpol for a red notice against Tulip Siddique.
Seven people are killed and two others are injured in a gas explosion at a house in Halishahar Thana, Chittagong.
Tarique Rahman is inaugurated as prime minister.
Six fishermen are abducted from a dry fish processing camp by pirates in Shelarchar in the East Sundarbans.
The World Health Organization confirms a fatal case of Nipah virus in Rajshahi Division.
Sheikh Hasina, Tulip Siddiq and two other relatives of the former prime minister are sentenced to up to 10 years' imprisonment over the illegal procurement of properties in Purbachal.
A fire breaks out at Camp 16 in Cox’s Bazar, destroying 335 shelters and displacing more than 2,000 Rohingya refugees.
The Border Guard Bangladesh detains 53 Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army members after they crossed into Bangladeshi territory amid fighting with the Arakan Army in Rakhine State, Myanmar.

The interim government bans the broadcasting of the 2026 Indian Premier League in Bangladesh following the exclusion of Bangladeshi cricketer Mustafizur Rahman from the Kolkata Knight Riders by the Board of Control for Cricket in India.
